subject: POC Planning: Acme Retail - proposed success criteria & scope adjustments
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@acmeretail.com>, Tom Gallagher <t.gallagher@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC Planning: Acme Retail - proposed success criteria & scope adjustments

Hi Hannah & Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on your Q3 roadmap and the priority to reduce cart abandonment on product pages. Per our discussion I put together a concise POC plan and the initial success criteria for the trial we've discussed. Attaching the plan and an evaluation spreadsheet with the proposed metrics.

High-level proposal (30-day trial):
- Primary use case: On-site product page assistant that answers product detail questions and suggests complementary items (goal: reduce time-to-first-engagement).
- Secondary use case: Cart abandonment assistant triggered on exit intent (goal: lift checkout completion by X%).
- Success metrics (proposed): baseline CTR on product recommendations, median first-reply latency, % of sessions with successful suggestion click, and end-to-end checkout conversion delta. Detailed formulas in attached evaluation_metrics_acme.xlsx.
- Data & access: sample anonymized product catalogue + 10k session logs (we described data needs on call).
- Owners: Acme product (Hannah) will validate business metrics; Redwood SE (Vivek) will onboard model & integration; Camila/Neha will handle success measurement and contract/ops.
- Timeline: Week 0 (kickoff & access), Week 1 (model baseline + sandbox), Week 2 (integration + QA), Week 3 (run & monitor), Week 4 (final analysis & recommendations).

Next steps I recommend this week:
1) Confirm the two data artifacts we need (product catalogue + sample session logs) and point of contact for secure transfer.
2) Agree on primary KPI to use for go/no-go at the end of the trial (I flagged conversion delta as the business KPI but we can re-baseline if you prefer engagement metrics).
3) NDA/POC paperwork if procurement needs it.

Attachments: Acme_POC_Plan_v1.pdf (POC scope, test cases, roles), evaluation_metrics_acme.xlsx (metrics + formulas).

If you'd like, I can sketch a shortened plan that focuses only on cart abandonment so we can run a tighter 2-week pilot instead — but I recommended the 30-day plan to get stable signals across both flows.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment: Acme_POC_Plan_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: evaluation_metrics_acme.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@acmeretail.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Gallagher <t.gallagher@acmeretail.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Planning: Acme Retail - proposed success criteria & scope adjustments

Camila — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Quick responses inline: 

- We like the two-use-case approach but need to add a lightweight personalization experiment. If the model can surface "people also viewed" suggestions that are personalized based on recent session signals, that's a higher priority for us than the product Q&A on some SKUs. Can we swap the primary/secondary roles so personalization is primary and cart-abandonment remains in scope?
- For success metric, marketing wants lift in add-to-cart rate for sessions that saw personalized suggestions (not just overall conversions). That means the evaluation spreadsheet will need a per-session attribution column.
- Data transfer: procurement is ok with a secure SFTP transfer. I'll loop in procurement for credentials but we can share a sanitized subset first.
- Timeline: moving the personalization experiment may require an extra 3 business days for us to prepare session metadata. Can you update the timeline and owners?

If this is doable, we want to proceed. Also, procurement will need a short statement of data handling — can you have a one-page note we can attach to the PO?

Thanks,
Hannah
Product Manager — Personalization | Acme Retail

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@acmeretail.com>, Tom Gallagher <t.gallagher@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Planning: Acme Retail - proposed success criteria & scope adjustments

Hi Hannah — great, thanks for the direction. We can absolutely reprioritize personalization as the primary use case. Updated notes below and explicit next steps so procurement and your engineering team have what they need.

Revised scope (30-day trial, re-baselined):
- Primary: Session-level personalization ("people also viewed" + contextual ranking) using recent session signals.
- Secondary: Cart-abandonment assistant as a fallback flow for exit-intent messaging.

Updated success criteria (high-level):
- Primary KPI: Add-to-cart rate lift among sessions exposed to personalized suggestions (compare holdout vs exposed).
- Secondary KPIs: Recommendation CTR, median model latency (ms), end-to-end conversion uplift.
- Evaluation detail: We'll add a session_id attribution column to the spreadsheet and include bootstrap confidence intervals in the final report.

Owners & responsibilities:
- Acme Product: Hannah (business acceptance, holdout definition)
- Acme Eng: Tom (SFTP credentials, integration point, event schema)
- Redwood SE: Vivek (sandbox onboarding, model tuning, latency profiling)
- Redwood AE: Camila & Neha (project management, metric collection, final analysis)

Revised timeline (estimate):
- Day 0 (Mon): Kickoff + SFTP credentials delivery
- Day 1–3: Data ingestion + sandbox mapping (Redwood SE + Acme Eng)
- Day 4–7: Model tuning & integration testing
- Day 8–24: Live trial (holdout/exposed split)
- Day 25–30: Analysis & wrap-up report

Procurement note: I'll have a one-page data handling statement prepared for you by EOD Monday. It will cover retention, encryption in transit & at rest, subset handling, and access controls (KMS/HSM mention).

Can you confirm: (1) SFTP point of contact and (2) whether Acme wants a 10% holdout by session or a smaller 5% holdout? Those affect required sample volumes.

If you confirm the SFTP contact and holdout percentage today, we can target a Monday kickoff.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Planning: Acme Retail - proposed success criteria & scope adjustments

Quick technical notes from the SE side: happy to proceed with the personalization-first plan. A few items to flag before kickoff: 

1) Session-level signals: please confirm the event names and whether session_id persists across devices. If not, we will need a sessionization step which adds 1–2 days.
2) Data samples: the 10k session logs you mentioned should include timestamp, session_id, item_id, event_type (view/add_to_cart), and anonymized user_id. A 1% sample is OK for initial tuning but we will need ~200k session events for statistically significant holdout analysis for a 5% holdout.
3) Integration: we can provide a lightweight SDK that calls the Redwood endpoint and returns ranked suggestions. Latency target: 120ms p99 for the ranking call; we can achieve this with the quantized Llama-2 variant if sequence lengths are bounded.
4) Security: SFTP is fine for bulk sample delivery. For live inference we'll recommend TLS + token-based auth and a VPC peering option if Acme prefers private connectivity.

I'll draft a short runbook for the ingestion steps and share it on the Drive link (same folder). Suggest we block a 60-min technical kickoff on Monday with Tom and their Eng lead to confirm event schema.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
